notes: Corrected to the verified native stack: upstream atomicarchitects/equiformer_v2@d5ad4be729b56f74012ebb7f097f77c5b00a1004 (main_oc20.py imports ocpmodels.common, registers nets/oc20.trainer). The only calculator is ocpmodels.common.relaxation.ase_utils.OCPCalculator bound to the provided equiformer_v2_153M_all_md.pt; the fairchem UMA / pretrained_mlip fallback has been removed entirely. Required modules are now ocpmodels, e3nn, ase, lmdb (aux: torch, numpy, yaml, pandas, pyarrow). doctor inspects the read-only input tree (manifest.json plus all declared files with basename fallback), imports every required and auxiliary module, verifies the OCPCalculator import, probes torch.cuda.is_available(), lists every missing item and exits 78 while anything is unavailable, otherwise 0. run exits 2 on missing CUDA (no CPU fallback) and 78 before loading any model when inputs are absent; with full assets it lowers the EquiformerV2 checkpoint via OCPCalculator, selects the two smallest-SHA256(sid) entries per OC20 validation partition from the LMDB, and performs genuine force-driven ASE relaxation with the fixed optimiser / fmax / max_steps / fixed-atom recipe from input/relaxation.yml, preserving atomic numbers, cell and fixed atoms (verified via recorded deltas). Outputs: relaxed_structures.extxyz, energies.parquet (sid/step/convergence), ranking.json, config.json (paths+SHA256), resume_state.json and per-sid work/ (final geometry, trajectory, optimiser log and optimizer.restart). resume reloads saved geometries and ASE restart files and continues only non-converged systems up to the declared total step budget. In this container assets_ready=false so doctor/run legitimately exit 78: a missing-asset report, not task completion.
